proof_boundary: Finite presentation sets and supplied observation lists define two explicit identity conventions. Supply preserves the observation list; profile equality matches SameProfile; profile-image cardinality is bounded by presentation cardinality; injective profiles make the conventions agree; unary-profile equality matches the imported Collapsed predicate. A closed fixture distinguishes the two conventions, so one Boolean evaluator cannot agree with both everywhere. This is model ambiguity, not a computability-theoretic undecidability theorem. The absent-convention query returns its tagged result even when its branch values agree. The trial-convention list is supplied data, not a checked transcription of trial files. The independent observation-family sweep uses carrier sizes 1 through 3, despite its introductory mention of 4; size 4 belongs to the separate unary-regime sweep.
